svg.title: A-103 Third Floor Plan — Detached Villa
svg.text: CANTILEVER — SINGLE ASYMMETRIC CURVE, 2.00 m WEST → 1.50 m EAST
Masonry wall cut by section — 200 mm
Internal stud or block partition, 120 mm
Single leaf door, swing shown to opening side
Glazed opening — arched head where noted
Element above the cut plane (pergola, slab
1. Final draft — layout agreed. The building is set back 1.00
m from the west, north and east boundaries; the south
faces the street across our own forecourt. Detaching costs
22% of the floor — 114.8 m² against 147.3 — and removes
the party wall, so one structural spine divides the plate.
2. Bedrooms are numbered 1 to 11 through the house, south to
north and west before east on each floor; the ground
floor's room is the guest bedroom and carries no number.
3. The west strip south of bedroom 9 is one room: no wall
divides the living area from the stair standing in it. The
stair is a private villa stair — 900 mm flights, 18R at
183 × 260 — needing no enclosure, no smoke vent and no
4. The south cantilever is reinforced concrete: one
asymmetric curve bowed outward, 2.00 m at the west end
sweeping away to 1.50 m at the east. Every point on the
edge stands outside the line joining the two ends.
5. East and north carry ordinary windows. The east neighbour
is a single storey in clay brick 1.00 m away, so they
clear its roof by 1.20 m at the first floor. The west is
louvred only — that neighbour is 3 storeys, and blind
6. Bedroom 8 and the shared bath open off the living area;
bedrooms 9 and 10 off the hall, whose dead end goes to
bedroom 9. Bedroom 10 has no balcony: it takes the north
Final draft — layout agreed with the client; not for construction.
Do not scale; work to figured dimensions only.
P13 2026-10-07 site plan redrawn for the detached villa
P14 2026-10-07 section A-A recut through the east strip, and marked on every plan
P15 2026-10-07 exterior: two schemes, elevations and balcony curves
P16 2026-10-07 neighbours as surveyed: west 3 storeys and blind, east single storey
